_purpose: Every wildcard surviving in the hardened policies must have an entry here, and every statement that grants MORE than the console original must be declared under intentional_grants. 22_iam_audit.py fails on anything undeclared. A missing entry is a failure, not a default pass -- that is the property the earlier draft lacked, which is how seven partial wildcards went uncounted while the summary claimed the gateway role had reached zero.

_classes.UNAVOIDABLE: The action does not support resource-level permissions. AWS rejects any Resource other than "*"; the grant cannot be scoped by policy at all.
_classes.SCOPED: The `*` covers only an opaque suffix, sub-resource, or AWS-owned field of one specific named resource. The statement does not reach a second resource of that type.
_classes.NECESSARY: The wildcard is broader than ideal and could not be narrowed. Requires an `evidence` pointer to an ablation run in which the narrowed or removed form was applied and the system demonstrably broke.

_account_portable: Patterns use * for the account field so the register survives a lab rebuild into a different account.

harness/BedrockMantleCallWithBearerToken.reason: Bearer-token exchange is an identity operation with no resource to name. `bedrock-mantle` is an undocumented internal service backing AgentCore inference; it publishes no resource-level ARNs for this action.

harness/EcrPublicTokenAccess.reason: `ecr-public:GetAuthorizationToken` returns a registry-wide credential and is documented by AWS as not supporting resource-level permissions.

harness/StsForEcrPublicPull.reason: STS bearer-token issuance takes no resource. Constrained in practice by the ECR Public pull it authorises, not by ARN.

harness/EcrManagedImageToken.reason: Same as the public variant: the authorization token is registry-scoped, and ECR does not accept a repository ARN on this action.

harness/XRayTracingAccess.reason: X-Ray segment ingestion has no resource model; AWS documents these four actions as requiring Resource "*". Write-only telemetry -- it cannot read traces.

harness/CloudWatchMetricsPublish.reason: PutMetricData supports no resource-level permission. Narrowed in practice by the cloudwatch:namespace condition key, which is the only available control.

kb/CloudWatchWritePermissionStatement.reason: Identical to the harness case: the knowledge base publishes ingestion metrics and PutMetricData cannot be resource-scoped.

harness/EcrManagedImagePull.reason: Repository prefix is pinned to `harness-*`. The remaining `*` is the ACCOUNT field, because AWS publishes AgentCore harness runtime images from an AWS-owned account whose ID is not documented. Read-only image pull; it cannot push or delete.

harness/AgentCoreWorkloadIdentity.reason: Scoped to this harness's own workload identity; the `*` covers only the generated suffix AgentCore appends to the harness name. It reaches no other workload.

harness/CloudWatchLogsGroup.reason: Restricted to AgentCore runtime log groups. Deliberately excludes /northstar-assist/model-invocations: the agent's identity must not be able to write to the log that records its own behaviour (threat R-02).

harness/CloudWatchLogsDescribeGroups.reason: Metadata read over runtime log groups only. Does not reach the model-invocation log group.

harness/CloudWatchLogsStream.reason: Write path for the runtime's own operational logs, scoped to runtime groups and their streams. The invocation audit log is out of reach by design.

harness/CloudWatchLogsPutResourcePolicy.reason: Tightest of the four: this harness's own runtime log group only.

gateway/GetGateway.reason: Scoped to this gateway; the `*` covers its own sub-resources. Read-only.

kb/S3GetObjectStatement.reason: Objects within the corpus bucket only -- the textbook least-privilege shape for this action, and further constrained by an aws:ResourceAccount condition. The console generated this correctly; hardening leaves it untouched.

harness/BedrockMantleInference.reason: PENDING ABLATION. `bedrock-mantle` is an undocumented internal service with no published resource ARNs, so no narrower form can be written. Must be shown necessary by removal test before this entry is valid.

gateway/GetConfigurationBundleVersion.reason: PENDING ABLATION. No configuration bundle is configured for this system, so the statement may have no caller at all and should be removed outright rather than justified.

gateway/AllowBedrockGetInferenceProfileF.reason: PENDING ABLATION. Read-only metadata. Should be scoped to the embedding model's profile ARN; ablation determines whether any profile is read at all.

gateway/AllowBedrockApplyGuardrailForKno.reason: A STANDARD-tier guardrail is invoked through a cross-Region guardrail PROFILE, and the profile ARN is regional and follows request routing. bedrock:ApplyGuardrail must therefore be granted on the profile in every region the profile routes to (us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2) or calls 403 intermittently. The console's sample policy grants only `guardrail/*` and cannot work at STANDARD tier.
gateway/AllowBedrockApplyGuardrailForKno.net_effect: Net narrowing. The guardrail dimension goes from `guardrail/*` -- every guardrail in the account -- to this one guardrail ID. The profile ARNs are a new resource TYPE that the original did not address, not a broadening of the original grant.
